title: The provider's unverified-sender refusal maps to a stable error code and does not leak the recipient
asA: operator running a deployed project where the sender domain has not yet been verified with the provider
iWant: the adapter to surface the refusal as a stable error class rather than a raw provider string
soThat: downstream code and log readers can act on the class without parsing provider prose

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the provider refuses the submission because the sender domain or address is unverified, the adapter returns the refusal outcome owned on TAC-401-email-smtp-resend-send-adapter.interfaces.send with the `RESEND_SENDER_UNVERIFIED` code from the classification owned on TAC-401-email-smtp-resend-send-adapter.responsibilities[3].
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running project whose configured from-address is not verified with the provider
acceptanceCriteria.when: the magic-link route calls `adapter.send({ to, subject, textBody, htmlBody })`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the returned object matches the refusal shape owned on TAC-401-email-smtp-resend-send-adapter.interfaces.send and its `error` begins with `RESEND_SENDER_UNVERIFIED`

acceptanceCriteria.description: On any adapter refusal, the recipient address, subject, and body do not appear on the returned `error` string, on the adapter's log stream during the call, or on any exception the adapter throws for the call.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a running project whose configured from-address is not verified with the provider and a distinctive recipient address the test can byte-scan for
acceptanceCriteria.when: the magic-link route calls `adapter.send({ to: distinctiveRecipient, subject: distinctiveSubject, textBody: distinctiveBody, htmlBody })` and the call resolves
acceptanceCriteria.then: the returned `error` string, every line the adapter emitted during the call, and every exception message caught contain none of the distinctive recipient, subject, or body substrings

acceptanceCriteria.description: The unverified-sender refusal maps to RESEND_SENDER_UNVERIFIED and does not surface the recipient identity: a probe of the returned error record shows only the stable code, the (redacted) provider response code and the sender placeholder reference; the recipient email is not on the error record even at debug level.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a send with an unverified sender configured and a recipient "recipient@example.test" and a caller reading the error record
acceptanceCriteria.then: the error carries code=RESEND_SENDER_UNVERIFIED and no field or nested field contains the string "recipient@example.test"; the sender placeholder reference name is present but the recipient email is not
